newsitem.title: MEXICO: Tropical Storm Andres due to land on Mexican coast.
newsitem.headline: Tropical Storm Andres due to land on Mexican coast.

text.p: Tropical Storm Andres was expected to land on Mexico's southern Pacific coast in Chiapas state by 1530 local (2130 GMT), the National Weather Service said here on Wednesday.
Andres abruptly switched direction late on Tuesday, heading east-northeast toward the Chiapas coast and passing by resort towns in Guerrero and Oaxaca.
"It is going to rain heavily in Chiapas and Oaxaca, especially around Tapachula," Televisa weatherman Enrique Albores said.
The city of Tapachula sits on the border with Guatemala and is one of Mexico's prime coffee growing regions.
Albores said the storm could get stronger, but he also said there was a chance it could veer even further from its current course to threaten Central America.
Andres was spotted heading and drawing heavy rains along the coasts of Oaxaca, Chiapas, Campeche and Tabasco, the National Weather Service said.
The storm was approaching at about 11 miles (16 km) per hour, with maximum winds of 40 miles (65 km) per hour and waves of up to 12 feet (4 meters), it said.

Resort towns of Acapulco, Puerto Angel and Huatulco reopened to small tourism and fishing ships after sailing was restricted on Tuesday, the Transportation and Communications Ministry shipping bulletin said.
Ships were warned to be cautious in sailing along Chiapas and Oaxaca and in the Gulf of Tehuantepec because of strong winds and high waves. ((--Timna Tanners, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7903))
